..
Another round of little to no rainfall is expected tonight, 
especially for the CNMI, as the current wedge of drier air lifts 
north. Then, Precipitable Water (PWAT) values of at least 2.0 inches
paired with light and variable winds will move over the region, so 
scattered island-effect showers in the afternoon are expected for 
Guam over the next couple of days. Next week, light to gentle trade 
winds will return to the region, so afternoon island-effect showers 
will be concentrated over the western shorelines and adjacent coastal
waters for Guam. Shower coverage will remain isolated for the CNMI 
throughout the forecast period.

Marine...
Combined seas are 5 to 7 FT and will remain as such through the 
forecast period. Model guidance shows another pulse in the long- 
period northwesterly swell emanating from Typhoon In-fa around Sunday
night and Monday, which would lead to advisory-level surf. 
Therefore, the High Surf Advisory and High Rip Current Risk Statement
were extended regardless of an expected dip in surf heights on 
Sunday. Surf observations today indicated surf of 7 to 9 FT along 
north and west facing reefs, so reflected those values in the 
forecast for tonight and Sunday night. In addition, a secondary trade
swell will build across the region next week, eventually becoming 
the dominant swell as In-fa and its respective swells continue moving
away to the north.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon In-fa is located around 21.4N 142.9E. As of 1:00 PM ChST,
In-fa was moving north-northwest at 13 MPH. Maximum sustained winds
are 130 MPH, making In-fa a low-end Category 4 typhoon. According to
the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) track, In-fa is forecast to
slowly stall and make a small clockwise loop before resuming its 
general motion towards the northern Pacific next week. Visible 
satellite imagery continues to show a well-defined eye with a near- 
symmetrical storm structure. Regardless, In-fa is forecast to
continue weakening over the next few days, possibly becoming a
Category 2 typhoon around Monday.

For more information please refer to bulletins from the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and from the National 
Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
The monsoon trough looks to settle south over the next few days,
likely stalling along a Pohnpei to Majuro line (or just south of
there). This limits surface convergence at both of those locations
after tonight, with just isolated showers expected most of the
forecast period. Farther south at Kosrae, with the trough just north
of you, you can expect to see scattered showers most of the forecast
this forecast period, with the exception being tonight when just 
isolated showers are expected.

For our mariners, look for light to gentle winds prevailing through
the forecast period, with seas of 4 to 6 feet expected.

Western Micronesia...
The monsoon trough borders the region, passing along 10N near
northern Yap State, before curving towards Typhoon In-fa to the
distant north. The next segment of the monsoon trough bends
southeastward to pass through Pohnpei State. The monsoon trough looks
to shift southward slightly, but convection is disorganized overall.
Isolated to scattered showers are expected over through much of the 
upcoming week for Yap and Palau. The segment of the trough moving 
towards Chuuk is expected to bring a period of scattered showers 
Sunday and Sunday night, with an area of showers persisting across 
southern Chuuk State on Monday and early Tuesday morning, along 
increased convergence on the southern side of the monsoon trough. 

Latest altimetry data shows combined seas of 3 to 5 feet, with seas
increasing to 6 ft north of Yap and Palau from a pulse of northeast  
swell from Typhoon In-fa. Seas will continue to build to 4 to 6 feet
across Yap and Palau, possibly reaching 7 feet at Yap early next 
week. Additionally, the long-period swell will also support elevated
surf along north-facing reefs over the next few days, with seas
possibly exceeding hazardous levels of 9 feet along north-facing 
reefs of Yap around Monday night or Tuesday. Meanwhile, benign seas 
and surf continue at Chuuk, with a slight increase in northeast swell
increasing seas to 4 to 6 feet around Tuesday.
